methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $25M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $1.8B.

data.narrative:
Atomic Industries is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Aaron Slodov, Austin Bishop, and Lou Young Jr., having raised $25M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 9 comparable companies—1 public and 8 private—including adjacent-stage peers Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B Series B), and Walden Robotics ($1.1B Seed).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, anchoring to $25M total raised as a proxy for current value, applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yielding $50M. Peer-median analysis across the 3 same-sector comparables produces $1.6B, reflecting the broader valuation range of $1.1B–$1.8B observed in the robotics manufacturing cohort. The divergence between methods reflects both the early stage of Atomic Industries relative to Series B peers and the typical variance in early-stage private company valuations.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $42.5M (conservative floor) to $1.9B (peer-based ceiling), with a median of $850M. This wide range reflects material uncertainty around Atomic Industries' relative progress within its cohort, execution risk at Series A, and the fact that peer valuations span seed through Series B stages. Resolution of this range will depend on demonstrable traction metrics and capital-efficiency relative to the peer set.
